subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should the remaining fix be a fresh current-main incremental session indexing implementation, a rescue of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179, or an intentional decision to keep full-entry reindexing for consistency?
rationale: The choice affects session-state correctness, schema semantics, batching behavior, and whether the conflicting candidate branch is worth adopting, which automation cannot decide safely.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and source-wide batching paths, with focused upgrade, overlap, and compaction coverage.

options.title: Rescue the open PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete assumptions before further review.

options.title: Keep full reindexing
options.body: Leave the existing full-entry behavior if maintainers decide consistency is worth the long-session indexing cost.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and source-wide batching paths, with focused upgrade, overlap, and compaction coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage/schema history makes this the best available owner for the schema-sensitive design choice.
